verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No τ_0 makes the Lean switch an instance of the paper's χ_t: timeSwitch vanishes on |t| ≤ 3/8, i.e. for 1 - t ≥ 5/8, which needs τ_0 ≥ 5/8, while it is known to equal 1 only for t ≥ 3/4, i.e. 1 - t ≤ 1/4, which needs τ_0/2 ≥ 1/4, so τ_0 ≤ 1/2 — and the paper additionally demands τ_0 < 1/2. The Lean switch is also only shown to vanish on a two-sided neighbourhood of 0 (|t| ≤ 3/8) rather than on all of 1 - t ≥ τ_0, i.e. nothing here rules out t < -3/8. The product c(x,t) = χ_x(x)χ_t(t) is never formed as a single function in Lean: the two cutoffs are applied in sequence (TimeLocalization.activatedVelocity applied to the spatially cut field), which is the same product pointwise. Rated low because both consequences the paper's proof draws from χ_t are stated for the Lean switch — the fields vanish near t = 0 (used for the initial-rest clause) and the switch is 1 on the late interval where the paper's and Lean's fields must agree (t ∈ [3/4, 1), as in PaperLocalization.local_theorem_with_compact_candidate) — and the numeric gap between 5/8 and 1/2 is a different admissible choice of constants, not a weaker statement, since the Lean never needs the support of c to sit inside the paper's Ω_*.
